newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed, no serious fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed, no serious fall seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Thursday with few Western orders, traders said.
The Russian Trading System of 24 shares fell by 0.04 percents to 174.26 on $9.47 million in volume.
Traders said the market would remain lethargic until President Boris Yeltsin undergoes a planned heart operation.
"Nothing will change before the president undergoes the operation," said Alexei Goncharov, head of the information department at Russian Brokerage House.
Doctors are due to meet on September 25 or 26 to decide when Yeltsin should have a bypass operation.
Goncharov said the market would not fall seriously, as shares falling 3.5 percent found support and rebounded.
He said the support level for Mosenergo was at $0.93, for UES at $0.076 and for Irkutskenergo at $0.100.
Ilya Sapozhnikov, a trader from Credit Suisse Moscow, said there was no clear trend on the market and brokers' attempts to make the market livelier were fruitless.

Goncharov said there were "amazing" trade volumes in KamAZ and Irkutskenergo. KamAZ volume was 677,000 shares in six deals, and Goncharov said that there were usually no more than two deals registered in the paper.
Irkutskenergo volume was 7.9 million, and Goncharov said the usual volumes was about two million.
He said someone was selling KamAZ shares for fear prices would go down further. KamAZ was the second biggest gainer of the day, closing at $1.45 after $1.39 at Wednesday's close.
The gainer of the day was St Petersburg Telephone, which was traded at $23.00 after $20.65.
Goncharov also noted "higher than usual" volumes in LUKoil. LUKoil volume was $2.04 million.
LUKoil said on Thursday that it signed a $5 billion joint venture agreement with Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) to undertake oil and gas projects in Russia and other countries.
But Goncharov did not see this linked with the high volumes.
Gazprom, which is planning an international share issue soon, has improved its performance on the market after it had announced new rules for re-registering shares, Goncharov said.
Gazprom was traded at $0.325 after $0320.
The loser of the day was Lenenergo, which closed at $0.372 after $0.394. The second biggest loser was Yuganskneftegaz, which fell to $7.700 from $8.113.
Goncharov said the forthcoming share issues discouraged investors in the shares.
Yuganskneftegaz parent company YUKOS said on Monday it planned to raise $300 million in three stock offerings to partically cover 4.35 trillion roubles in debt.
"If they make the issues, it will crash the market in the share," Goncharov said. "There will be quite a few people who will give up the share altogether."
Mosenergo rose to $0.948 from $0.944, UES was unchanged at $0.0770 and Rostelekom rose to $2.52 from $2.50.
--Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
